evidence.claim: Galaxy says remaining TCEQ permits do not gate Helios construction or energization and the Texas permitting freeze will not affect Helios timelines; permits for current builds are in hand.
evidence.numbers: ERCOT Batch Zero gave conditional classification to ~4.2 GW across five Galaxy projects (>1.6 GW at Helios I-II); Caspian's reconsideration was denied; 2.6 GW sits in study load, with clarity around April 2027 and audit results in December.

evidence.claim: 3Q26 10-Q: air permits for larger installations are taking longer than expected, and construction, land-use and gas permits have also been delayed; Bloom generally cannot sell its Energy Servers to a financier until permits are in hand.
evidence.numbers: Permits now gate revenue recognition for financier-bought systems; Jupiter (Oracle, New Mexico) was not mentioned on the call; hearing set for 7 December (press).

evidence.claim: Amazon withdrew its four-building Ashburn, Virginia campus at the former GWU site after resident and county opposition, ceding about 25 acres and $5M to the county.
evidence.numbers: Amazon paid $427M for the 122-acre site in March.

evidence.claim: Trump urged data centers to pay communities a dividend and make their own power; Hazle Township residents earlier rejected an AWS campus despite a $10,000-per-resident offer.
evidence.numbers: Cash offers are not reliably buying consent.

evidence.claim: Memphis council rejected an 18-month moratorium on a 6-6 vote but approved a 135-day pause on new data center applications alongside a 90-day review; SpaceXAI's turbines remain the flashpoint.
Moratorium bills failed in about ten states, including vetoes in Maine and Vermont.
Ordered a grid audit in August and paused environmental permits for AI and crypto data centers in September.
Brian Janous says polling turned sharply negative from about September 2025; gas plants draw more opposition than data centers.
Paused state environmental permits for new data centers of 50 MW or more for up to a year.

Asked about permitting and counterparty credit for slots out to 2029-30, the CEO said Caterpillar is 'not seeing significant changes' in customer project timing, but declined to say what share of slots hyperscalers back.
evidence.numbers: No deferrals disclosed; backlog grew $5.9bn QoQ. Management's words and the numbers agree for now, but disclosure is thin.

question: Is opposition slowing builds, and where?
summary: Opposition is now national politics: Amazon dropped a Virginia campus, Memphis paused applications for 135 days, and Trump is telling developers to pay communities and make their own power. Moratorium bills mostly fail, but local pauses and withdrawals are rising, and cash offers have not reliably won votes.
title: Permitting and community backlash
